fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Then the passage says, "As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders." (Micah 7:15). It looks back to the days of coming out of Egypt. And the word it lands on is wonders.

That's right, friend. The speaker says, "Though I have fallen, I will arise…" (Micah 7:8). The enemy is told not to gloat, because the fall isn't the last word. I think that's a pretty bold thing to say to an enemy.

Rock is a strong word, friend, but it isn't the one here. The speaker says, "though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light." (Micah 7:8). Light is the answer that matches the dark. A rock in a dark room just gives you something to stub your toe on.

Not this time, friend. The verse says "The day for rebuilding your walls will come—the day for extending your boundary." (Micah 7:11). The verse is about rebuilding the walls. Someone who abandons a wall doesn't go on to extend the boundary.

Walls showed up a couple of verses earlier, so I see the connection. But verse 11 was about rebuilding them, and verse 13 gives a different reason. The earth becomes desolate "…because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds." (Micah 7:13).

Laws is a fair guess, friend, so I see why you reached for it. But the verse doesn't say laws. Then the passage says, "As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders." (Micah 7:15).

Riches would be nice, friend. I'd settle for a bigger oven. But that's not what this verse promises. Then the passage says, "As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders." (Micah 7:15). The word is wonders.

That's right, friend. Verse 17 says, "They will come trembling from their strongholds in the presence of the LORD our God; they will tremble in fear of You." The dust-licking and the trembling are in the very same verse. So the statement is true.
The wilderness is a good guess, friend, but it isn't the place in this verse. Micah 7:19 says, "You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea." So the sins go into the depths of the sea.

Behind His back is a nice picture, friend, but it isn't the one in this verse. Micah 7:19 says, "You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea." That's a whole lot of water. The answer is the depths of the sea.

Right, friend. The message ends with God showing "…faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old." (Micah 7:20). The promise goes back to the days of old. So it isn't something new.
